transcript:
[00:00] Sam (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick check in, only 45 minutes on the calendar. Maya, Alex, Diego from FinApp, is that right?...
[00:08] Alex (FinApp - Eng Lead): Yep that's us. We also have Maya on product. Diego from security will jump in for the second half.
[00:13] Priya (Redwood SE): Hi all, Priya here. I'll walk through the SDK changes and the structured output mapping we pushed yesterday.
[00:20] Maya (FinApp - PM): Cool, thanks. We ran the initial end-to-end yesterday but saw a couple of anomalies in the JSON output shape — sometimes arrays are null.
[00:29] Priya: Yeah that's one of the things we patched; it was a serialization edge when a field is optional and the SDK v0.9.3 returned undefined versus empty array. We pushed v0.9.4 that coerces to [] for optional arrays.
[00:42] Alex: Nice. Where can we pull that? We tried pip install but cached the older wheel.
[00:47] Sam: I'll post the direct wheel and a small code snippet in the notes after the call. Also we added server-side compatibility so older clients don't break.
[00:55] [00:55] Priya: On the structured output, we adopted a top-level "result" object with items[] and metadata. Example: {result:[...], metadata:{confidence, provenance}} — again the lib will always send items:[] even if empty.
[01:12] Alex: That helps. One question: our app expects tool calling to include an id and typed params. How do you map that in the SDK?
[01:20] Priya: We expose ToolCall objects in the SDK: tool_call.id, tool_call.name, tool_call.params (typed dict), and tools can be registered with a handler. In JS we showed the callback example. In Python it's similar, register_tool('get_account', handler_func).
[01:38] Maya: On the get_account example, we noticed a 200ms variance — sometimes response from the tool handler took longer and the model timed out. Any recommendations?
[01:47] Priya: We have two suggestions: 1) async tool handlers with streaming resume so the model stream isn't blocked; 2) increase tool timeout and enable optimistic caching so the runtime returns cached responses for common account queries.
[02:01] Alex: Is optimistic caching enabled by default for Dedicated?
[02:05] Sam: On Dedicated you can opt into aggressive prefix KV caching. Hosted defaults to conservative caching for fresh data safety.
[02:13] Diego: Quick security question — where is the cache stored? We can't have PII in plaintext.
[02:19] Priya: For Private/Dedicated we support customer-managed KMS and encrypted KV. For hosted it's encrypted at rest with our KMS; we also provide redaction hooks and a policy to disable caching for sensitive routes.
[02:32] Diego: Good. We'll need to see the encryption at rest docs and the KMS flow — which providers do you support?
[02:38] Sam: We support AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault, and external HSMs through our private deployment. I'll add the security doc link after the call.
[02:47] [03:00] Priya: Back to the integration: we saw you ran the sample workload for 1k requests, what was the latency distribution? Alex?
[03:08] Alex: P95 was around 420ms on hosted with the quantized model, P50 ~160ms. But we saw tail spikes to 1.2s during bursts.
[03:17] Priya: Bursts likely from concurrent tool calls causing extra blocking. For that we recommend batch window tuning and increasing worker threads on the handler side.
[03:27] Maya: Is there a quick config to change batch window without redeploy?
[03:31] Priya: Yes, the runtime supports dynamic config via the console API. We can change batch_window_ms and worker_pool_size; I'll include the API curl in the notes.
[03:40] Alex: One more perf nuance: we ran with a 1024 seq length but typical user prompts are 256; do you have guidance on token limits for cost vs latency?
[03:49] Priya: If majority are 256, pin the model to a shorter context optimized kernel and enable prefix KV caching to avoid re-encoding unchanged context. That gives better token throughput and lower cost.
[04:02] [04:15] Sam: On the billing side, for the pilot you can mix hosted at on-demand pricing and Dedicated reserved for heavy routes. We'll prepare a blended cost estimate based on your 5k daily requests profile.
[04:22] Alex: Please do. Also include embedding costs for our search rerank path.
[04:26] Priya: Quick question from my side: are you planning to use function/tool calling extensively for transactional flows or mostly for enrichment?
[04:34] Maya: Mostly transactional for payment routing and account lookups; enrichment for UX copy and summaries.
[04:40] Priya: Then we should prioritize low-latency Dedicated paths for the transactional routes and hosted for enrichment where cost matters more.
[04:49] [05:00] Diego: Security follow-ups: we need SOC 2 attestation and audit logs for data access. Do you ship audit logs per request?
[05:07] Sam: Yes, we produce per-request trace logs and you can push them to your SIEM; for Private deployments we can stream logs to customer S3/Cloud Storage. For Hosted we provide export hooks and retention controls.
[05:18] Diego: And SSO? We need SAML SSO and SCIM for user provisioning.
[05:23] Sam: SAML + SCIM supported. I'll send our SAML metadata and the SCIM endpoint docs.
[05:28] Alex: Great. Back to the SDK, we hit a bug where the Python client reserialized numbers as strings in the params object.
[05:36] Priya: Oof, that is the JSON encoder we used for older Python versions; v0.9.4 includes a stricter encoder that preserves numeric types. Please confirm after you pull the new wheel.
[05:45] Maya: We'll test. Also we need the structured output schema to include an errors[] array with codes so our client can decide retry vs escalate.
[05:54] Priya: That's on the schema — we'll add errors as an array of {code, message, retriable} and ensure it's present even if empty. SDK will map to typed Error objects.
[06:07] Alex: Any plan for model rollouts? We want canary so we don't break prod.
[06:11] Sam: Yes, rollouts and canary flags supported at route level. You can route X% to canary model and auto-fallback on regressions. We'll include a sample rollout policy in the notes.
[06:23] [06:30] Priya: Quick demo note: we attempted to reproduce your failing prompt and saw one output where the model hallucinated an account number. We added a post-process redaction step in the SDK to remove sequences that match account regexes.
[06:44] Maya: That's reassuring. Will that redaction affect the structured output fields like account_id if present?
[06:49] Priya: No, redaction runs only on free text outputs; structured fields are validated against expected patterns and sanitized differently. We'll show examples.
[06:58] Diego: For compliance, can you set retention to 30 days and ensure deletion on request? Also need deletion logs for audit.
[07:06] Sam: Yes, retention policy configurable per-route. Delete events are logged and can be pushed to your audit storage. We'll include the procedure.
[07:15] [07:30] Alex: On the performance baseline, Priya, can you outline what your script measures so we can replicate locally?
[07:36] Priya: It measures cold-start latency, p50/p95/p99 for generation, tool call latency, and end-to-end total. It also reports token throughput and cost estimate using our blended pricing model.
[07:48] Alex: Good. We'll run it against both hosted and dedicated endpoints.
[07:52] Maya: Anything else on observability? We need per-route token breakdown for cost allocation.
[07:58] Sam: Console has per-route token breakdown and tag-based cost allocation. We'll demo that in follow-up and share screenshots.
[08:08] [08:20] Priya: Quick triage on structured output mismatch you reported: Example conversation id typed as int vs string; we recommend normalizing to string to avoid cross-language issues.
[08:31] Alex: Ok we'll normalize client side, but prefer server send string to be consistent.
[08:36] Priya: We'll make that change in the schema v1.2 and bump the SDK compatibility flag.
[08:42] Maya: Anything blocking the pilot progression from Redwood side?
[08:46] Sam: No blockers. From FinApp, dependencies are security questionnaire and perf runs.
[08:52] Maya: Timeline check — we aim for a limited internal pilot by end of month. Does that align?
[08:57] Priya: Yes, if action items complete this week we can support that timeline.
[09:02] Alex: Let's talk benchmarks: we'll run 5k requests/day with peak 200rps bursts. Expectation: p95 < 600ms on transactional routes.
[09:13] Priya: That is doable with Dedicated and tuning. We'll provide config recommendations.
[09:20] Sam: Next steps recap — we'll post SDK wheel, schema, rollout example, security docs, and perf script. Are we agreed?
[09:27] All: Yes.
[09:30] [09:35] Sam: Okay closing notes — I'll open a ticket in the trial workspace for all artifacts and add deadlines. Thanks everyone.
[09:40] Alex: Thanks.
[09:42] Maya: Thanks.
[09:43] Diego: Bye.
